program_name: Cultural Heritage and Creativity for Tourism and Territorial Development (official English name; the UNITO microsite and Italian register also write it as 'Cultural Heritage and Creativity for tourism and territorial development' / 'Patrimonio culturale e creativita per il turismo e lo sviluppo territoriale'). UNITO course code 2608M22; Apply@UniTo course id 694.
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). It is a stand-alone Italian second-cycle degree (laurea magistrale, LM-49) delivered 100% in English; it is not an English pathway/curriculum inside an Italian-named degree, and it is not a joint/interuniversity degree with another university. The programme microsite 'Key information' records 'Language: English' for every academic year listed (2022/2023, 2023/2024, 2024/2025) and Apply@UniTo records 'Study language: English'. It IS however an inter-departmental degree inside UNITO: the reference department is the Department of Historical Studies, with Humanities, the Interuniversity Department of Regional and Urban Studies and Planning (DIST - 'Scienze, Progetto e Politiche del Territorio'), Management 'Valter Cantino', Foreign Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures, Philosophy and Education Sciences, and Earth Sciences also involved. DIST is formally a UNITO-Politecnico di Torino joint department, but the degree itself is awarded by UNITO alone. The final dissertation is written in English; teaching is described as 'blended'.
campus: Biella, Piedmont (NOT Turin). The programme microsite states 'Teaching Location: Biella (UNESCO creative city)' and has a whole 'Living in Biella' navigation section; Apply@UniTo states 'Study location: Italy, Biella'. Teaching is hosted at the Citta Studi Biella campus (about 80 km north-east of Turin). The Apply@UniTo page header nevertheless shows the university's own seat, 'Italy, Turin - Department of Historical Studies', which is the administering department in Turin, not the teaching seat.
degree_class: LM-49 - Progettazione e gestione dei sistemi turistici (Class of master's degrees in Planning and Management of Tourism Systems). 120 ECTS/CFU, 2 years. UNITO programme code 2608M22; en.unito.it degree id 45792; AlmaLaurea codicione 0010107305000001.
admission_type: Open (free / non-restricted) access - 'The Master's Degree Program has non-restricted access' / 'Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale e ad accesso non programmato'. There is no numerus clausus for Italian/EU applicants and no ranking-based competition, but enrolment is conditional on a MANDATORY PRELIMINARY ADMISSION APPLICATION ('domanda di ammissione preliminare', submitted through a dedicated online procedure) that is assessed by a Selection Committee of at least three programme teachers. Candidates who hold a bachelor's degree in the humanities or economic-managerial-legal area AND the 48-ECTS curricular requirements AND an English B2 certificate are admitted directly; all others are called to an online oral interview. For non-EU applicants residing abroad a territorial quota does apply: Apply@UniTo states 'This Master's degree program has 85 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' [uncertain - Apply@UniTo's entry-qualification section states more broadly that 'Prospective students will be interviewed by a commission that will evaluate the candidates' applications on the ground of the submitted documents', which reads as if every international applicant is interviewed, whereas the programme microsite grants direct admission without interview to candidates who already meet all requirements; the two official pages are not fully consistent]
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027, applicants with a FOREIGN qualification who are Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents or non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy (Apply@UniTo): two possible windows - (a) First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes); (b) Fourth admission call, reserved to open-access postgraduate degree programmes and to Italians/EU/EU-equivalents/non-EU legally residing in Italy, 25 August - 8 September 2026; the course page shows the hard deadline as '8 Sept 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time'. A non-refundable EUR 60 application fee must be paid within the deadline of each call (same amount whether one or two programmes are selected). Applicants holding an ITALIAN qualification do not use Apply@UniTo: they submit the preliminary admission application ('ammissione preliminare') on the UNITO online procedure and then enrol through MyUniTO within the windows published on the programme's 'How to apply' page. For the previous cycle (a.y. 2025/2026) the programme page listed 'Application periods for EU, equivalents, non-EU Citizens legally residing in Italy: November 26th 2024 - January 30th 2025' and 'August 21st 2025 - September 4th 2025'. [uncertain - the programme microsite is unreachable, so its own 2026/2027 window listing and the exact preliminary-admission / interview dates for 2026/2027 could not be read; the dates above are the university-wide Apply@UniTo calls confirmed on the live course page and the live apply.unito.it calendar]
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027, non-EU citizens residing abroad (visa applicants): the ONLY usable Apply@UniTo window was the First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, which is the single call 'open to all applicants wishing to apply for postgraduate degree programs'. The later calls (third, fourth and fifth) are explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy', and the 8 September 2026 deadline currently displayed on the course page carries the notice 'This call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.' In addition, admitted non-EU applicants needing a study visa must submit the pre-enrolment application on the Universitaly platform (one programme only, choosing the competent Italian embassy/consulate) by 15 July 2026 for a.y. 2026-2027. The equivalent window for the previous cycle was 'Application deadline for NON-EU Citizens residing abroad: January 30th 2025'. As of the research date (1 September 2026) the 2026/2027 non-EU-abroad window is closed; the corresponding first call for a.y. 2027/2028 would be expected around late November 2026 - late January 2027 but is not yet published. Quota: 85 places for non-European applicants residing abroad. [uncertain - the 2027/2028 dates are an expectation based on the recurring pattern, not published information]
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination, no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT. Selection is document-based, carried out by a Selection Committee ('Commissione') made up of at least three teachers of the programme, on the basis of the preliminary admission application. Two outcomes: (1) candidates holding a bachelor's degree in a humanities or economic-managerial-legal class WHO ALSO meet the 48-ECTS curricular requirement AND hold an English certificate of at least B2 'will be admitted directly' (no interview); (2) candidates coming from other degree classes, or not meeting the minimum curricular requirements, or without an English certificate, must sit an ONLINE ORAL INTERVIEW, notified in advance by e-mail, in which the Committee checks the adequacy of prior knowledge and skills, verifies English proficiency where no certificate was submitted, and may prescribe one or two 'realignment' classes ('Fundamentals, lexicon and methods of the arts'; 'Fundamentals of economic sciences and land management') and/or single courses to be taken to fill missing credits. A MOTIVATION LETTER is a compulsory part of the application ('Other requirements: A motivation letter must be added to your application' - Apply@UniTo). Candidates receive the Committee's decision by notice at the end of the evaluation, according to the deadlines posted on the programme website. [uncertain - Apply@UniTo phrases the interview as applying to all prospective (international) students, while the programme microsite limits it to candidates who do not already satisfy all requirements; the live microsite could not be opened to confirm which rule is applied to Apply@UniTo candidates in 2026/2027]
academic_requirements:
1) QUALIFICATION. A first-cycle degree (bachelor's / laurea triennale) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable under current Italian regulations. Three-year academic diplomas from Italian Conservatories and Academies of Fine Arts (and equivalent foreign Arts Academy / Music Conservatory BAs) are expressly accepted.
2) SUBJECT AREA. Preferably a bachelor's degree in a class of the humanities area or of the economic-managerial-legal area; degrees from other classes are also accepted, provided the curricular credit requirement below is met.
3) CURRICULAR CREDITS. A minimum of 48 CFU/ECTS (or the rough foreign equivalent) in the scientific-disciplinary sectors characterising the LM-49 class, covering AT LEAST THREE of the following seven disciplinary areas: (a) History - L-ANT/02, L-ANT/03, L-ANT/07, L-ANT/08, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/04, M-STO/06, SECS-P/12; (b) Art History - L-ART/01, L-ART/02, L-ART/03, L-ART/04; (c) Media and Performing Arts - L-ART/05, L-ART/06, L-ART/07; (d) Foreign Languages - L-LIN/04, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/09, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/14; (e) Economy and Management - SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/10; (f) Law and Social Sciences - IUS/01, IUS/04, IUS/06, IUS/09, IUS/13, IUS/14, M-PSI/05, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/05, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10; (g) Geography and Landscape sciences - BIO/07, GEO/04, ICAR/06, ICAR/15, M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, SECS-S/04.
4) PERSONAL PREPARATION. Adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation with respect to the educational objectives of the programme, including English proficiency at B2 or equivalent, verified by the Selection Committee.
5) GAP-FILLING. 'Candidates not meeting the minimum requirements may be directed by the teaching staff to relevant classes offered by the University of Torino, in order to fill any gaps in their preparation' - in practice one or two 'realignment' courses and/or single courses ('corsi singoli') prescribed at the interview.
6) NO PUBLISHED GPA / MINIMUM GRADE THRESHOLD. None of the official UNITO sources consulted sets a minimum bachelor's GPA or final mark.
7) PLACES. Open access for Italians / EU / EU-equivalents / non-EU legally residing in Italy (no cap published). Non-EU applicants residing abroad: 85 places (a.y. 2026/2027, Apply@UniTo 'Territory requirements'). No Marco Polo quota is published for this programme.
8) TIMING. Applicants who have already graduated, or who expect to graduate by the end of December, must submit the preliminary admission application through the dedicated online procedure BEFORE starting the enrolment procedure.
language_requirements: ENGLISH - CEFR B2 minimum, evidenced by an international certificate. Accepted certifications and minimum scores as published on Apply@UniTo for this programme: Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); Cambridge First Certificate in English (FCE) with a minimum score of 173 (grade B); PTE Academic, minimum 65; IELTS, minimum 5.5 out of 9 with no component below 5.5; TOEFL iBT, minimum 69 out of 120 with no component below 17; Trinity College ISE II. ALTERNATIVE / EXEMPTION: 'applicants have to upload an official document issued by their previous University stating that the medium of instruction was English' (medium-of-instruction letter) instead of a certificate. A further de facto route exists for candidates without any certificate: the Selection Committee verifies English proficiency directly during the online oral interview ('The Committee will also verify - in case of the absence of the relevant certification - the knowledge of the English language'). ITALIAN is NOT required for admission: the UNITO Italian B2 requirement applies only to non-EU visa applicants enrolling in ITALIAN-taught free-access programmes, which this programme is not. Free Italian language courses are offered to enrolled students (the microsite has a dedicated 'Learning Italian' page), and knowledge of a second foreign language is developed inside the curriculum rather than required at entry. [uncertain - it could not be verified on the live microsite whether the accepted-certificate list and score thresholds were updated for a.y. 2026/2027; the list above is the one published on the live Apply@UniTo course page for intake 2026/27]
required_documents:
A) THROUGH APPLY@UNITO (applicants with a foreign qualification): 1) valid passport (non-EU citizens) or valid ID card (Italians, EU citizens and equivalents); 2) for non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, a residence permit valid for university enrolment; 3) first-cycle degree certificate (bachelor's diploma) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, signed/sealed and with proof of authenticity - or, if not yet graduated, an official enrolment certificate stating the expected qualification; 4) official transcript of records / study plans evidencing the minimum 48 ECTS across at least three of the required disciplinary areas (plus any intermediate academic qualification and its study plan); 5) MOTIVATION LETTER (explicitly compulsory for this programme: 'Other requirements: A motivation letter must be added to your application'), in English; 6) English language certificate from the accepted list, or an official medium-of-instruction letter from the previous university; 7) Curriculum Vitae; 8) certified translation of any document not issued in English, French, Italian or Spanish (entry-qualification documents are accepted as-is in those four languages; otherwise both original and certified translation must be uploaded); 9) payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call. Optional but frequently requested afterwards by the International Students Office: Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) or CIMEA Statement of Comparability / Statement of Verification, and an explanation of the grading system. Documents without signature, seal or stamp are not accepted and incomplete applications are not considered.
B) THROUGH THE UNITO PRELIMINARY-ADMISSION ONLINE PROCEDURE (applicants with an Italian qualification, and the documentation the Selection Committee assesses): degree certificate or self-certification of the degree/enrolment, transcript of records documenting the 48 ECTS, English language certification (or declaration), CV and identity document.
C) FOR NON-EU VISA APPLICANTS, in addition: the Universitaly pre-enrolment (visa) application by 15 July 2026, and the documents required by the competent Italian embassy/consulate for the study visa. [uncertain - the itemised list for section A/B is reconstructed from the live Apply@UniTo course page (items 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 are stated there or in its entry-qualification/other-requirements blocks) combined with the university-wide 'Required documents for international students' page on en.unito.it, which is behind Cloudflare and could only be read through search-engine extracts; a programme-specific document checklist on the microsite could not be opened]

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCESS PROBLEM. www.culturalheritage.unito.it, en.unito.it and www.unito.it could not be reached live during this research: direct HTTPS requests to the culturalheritage.unito.it origin hung and timed out from every path tried (WebFetch, curl with a desktop User-Agent, r.jina.ai - the latter returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge), and en.unito.it returned HTTP 403 even with browser User-Agent headers. Only apply.unito.it (hosted externally on the DreamApply platform) responded live and is therefore the primary verified source for a.y. 2026/2027. The programme microsite content was recovered from Wayback Machine snapshots: 'How to apply' of 26 March 2025, 'Admission requirements' of 21 May 2025 (a.y. 2025/2026 content), 'Key information' of 26 March 2025 (with 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25 tabs), and the microsite homepage of 5 May 2026. No 2026/2027 snapshot of the admission-requirements page exists, so the curricular/interview rules quoted are the most recent published version (2025/2026) and were cross-checked against the LIVE Apply@UniTo course page, where they appear essentially unchanged (same 48-ECTS rule, same seven disciplinary areas, same bachelor-class wording).
2) CAMPUS DISCREPANCY (resolved). The Apply@UniTo page header shows 'Italy, Turin - Department of Historical Studies' while its own key-facts block shows 'Study location: Italy, Biella'. The programme microsite is unambiguous: 'Teaching Location: Biella (UNESCO creative city)', with a whole 'Living in Biella' section. The teaching seat is BIELLA (Citta Studi Biella); the administering department sits in Turin. This is a genuine trap for applicants who assume the programme is in Turin.
3) TEACHING LANGUAGE. Unambiguously and fully English-taught, single-university (UNITO) degree - not a pathway inside an Italian-named degree. Note however that it is strongly inter-departmental (seven UNITO departments, one of which, DIST, is a UNITO-Politecnico di Torino joint department); this does not make the DEGREE interuniversity, and the diploma is awarded by UNITO alone.
4) ADMISSION TYPE NUANCE. 'Open access' is accurate in the Italian sense (accesso non programmato, no ranking, no numerus clausus for domestic/EU applicants) but is NOT unconditional: the preliminary admission application and Selection Committee evaluation are mandatory, and a hard quota of 85 places applies to non-EU applicants residing abroad. Applicants should not read 'free admission' as 'automatic admission'.
5) INTERVIEW SCOPE INCONSISTENCY. The microsite says candidates who already meet all requirements (right bachelor's class + 48 ECTS + B2 certificate) 'will be admitted directly', with the online oral interview reserved to everyone else. Apply@UniTo instead states flatly that 'Prospective students will be interviewed by a commission'. International applicants should assume an interview may be scheduled.
6) 2026/2027 PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DATES. The microsite's own 'How to apply' page was last recoverable in its 2025/2026 version (last update 07/02/2025). The 2026/2027 dates given in this record come from the live Apply@UniTo course page and the live 'When can I apply?' calendar; the programme's internal preliminary-admission windows and Committee notification dates for 2026/2027 could not be read.
7) TIMING CAVEAT. As of the research date (1 September 2026) the a.y. 2026/2027 cycle is essentially over for non-EU applicants residing abroad (their only window closed 29 January 2026) and closes on 8 September 2026 for EU/equivalent applicants. Anyone planning for 2027/2028 should expect the first (all-applicants) postgraduate call to open around late November 2026, but those dates are not yet published.
8) FEES. The EUR 2,800/year figure is the top of the 2025-26 income-based range (EUR 156-2,800); 2026-27 amounts are published separately on the UNITO fees pages and, for international students, depend on the GDP per capita (PPP) of the country of residence. No extra programme-specific contribution is advertised for this degree. Part-time enrolment is available and changes the fee.
9) LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE LIST. Taken verbatim from the live Apply@UniTo course page for intake 2026/27 and therefore current, but the programme's own admission-requirements page (unreachable) states only the generic 'B2 or at least a corresponding level'; if the two ever diverge, the Apply@UniTo list is the operative one for international applicants.
10) REQUIRED DOCUMENTS. The university-wide checklist for postgraduate international applicants on en.unito.it could not be opened directly (Cloudflare 403 live; Wayback repeatedly rate-limited with HTTP 429 during this session) and was reconstructed from search-engine extracts of that page plus the live Apply@UniTo course page. The programme-specific mandatory items (bachelor's degree, transcript proving 48 ECTS, English certificate or medium-of-instruction letter, motivation letter, EUR 60 fee) are all directly confirmed on the live Apply@UniTo page.
